1 By this judgment I will dispose of appeal u/sec.374 Cr.PC. filed on behalf of convict Dinesh Yadav against the judgment dated 13.02.2014 and order on sentence dated 20.02.2014 passed by Sh.
Gaurav Rao, Ld. ACMM-II, Patiala House Court, New Delhi.

2 The brief facts of the case as per record and from trial court CA No. 20/16 Dinesh Yadav Vs. State  R/O 38 vs The State (Delhi Administration) on 14 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23115013/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: record are that accused is running an establishment namely M/s Shri Bankey Bihari Sweets, at shop no. B-6/170, Sector-7, Rohini, Delhi-85.

On 25.07.2007 at about 11.45 a.m. Food Inspector Sh.
Sanjeev Kumar Gupta visited the said place and purchased 1500 grams of "Bundi Ke Ladoo" from accused.
FI was accompanied with SDM/LHA Sh. M. K. Dwiivedi.
The said Bundi Ke Ladoo was purchased for the purposes of analysis under PFA Act.
The same sample was divided into three parts, packed as per Rules of PFA.
Panchanama was prepared.
One sample was sent for analysis to Public Analyst.

As per the report of Analyst, sample did not confirm to the standard because "The sample does not conform to standard because total dye content of synthetic colour used exceeds the prescribed maximum limit of 100 PPM (158.90 PPM)."
3
As the sample was failed, prosecution was launched by Food Inspector by filing complaint dated 31.10.2007 with the court.
Accused was summoned.
He has exercised his right u/sec.13(2) PFA Act to get the sample analyzed by CFL.

CFL reported "I am of the opinion that the sample contains synthetic food colour more than 100 PPM and hence Rule 30 of PFA Rules, 1955 (156.81 PPM)."
4
Charge was framed against accused u/sec.2(ia) (a) (j) (m) read with sec.7 of PFA Act, 1954 punishable u/sec.16(1A) of PFA Act.

5 After trial, vide judgment dated 13.02.2014 accused was convicted for offence u/sec.16(1A) of PFA Act and vide order on sentence dated 20.02.2014, accused was directed to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 18 months and fine of Rs.10,000/- and in default of payment of fine SI of 60 days.
CA No. 20/16 Dinesh Yadav Vs. State

6 In this appeal, the accused has assailed the judgment on the following grounds:-
(i) Non-compliance of Sec.10(7) of PFA Act and Rule i.e. independent witnesses were not joined.
(ii) There is variation in different reports (PA and CFL) so the sample was not properly homogenized.
(iii) Non-compliance of Rule 14 of PFA Rules i.e. the bottles, spoon, tray were not made clean and dried at the spot by the food inspector or any other official.
7 No reply was filed by respondent/state and the matter was argued orally.
8 I have gone through the record, Trial Court record and have heard the submissions of Ld. counsel for appellant and Ld. SPP for State.
It is argued by counsel for appellant that no public witness was present in the proceedings nor efforts were made to join any public witnesses.
As far as this argument is concerned, the same argument was raised before the Ld. Trial Court.
The same was dealt by the trial court from para 21 to 24 of the judgment.

As far as opinion/finding of the trial R/O 38 vs The State (Delhi Administration) on 14 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23115013/
2 court regarding this argument is concerned, I do not find any infirmity in those findings and the same are upheld and the arguments regarding this fact does not find any force and thus rejected.
9 It is further stated that there is variation in the report of PA and CFL and due to that reason benefit goes in favour of the accused.
This line of argument was done before the trial court and was dealt in para 61 to 87 of the judgment.
I do not want to differ from the reasoning given by the trial court and thus the same is upheld.
CA No. 20/16 Dinesh Yadav Vs.
State  10
It is further argued that compliance u/sec.14 PFA Rules was not proved on record by the prosecution.
It is stated that witnesses are deposing differently with respect to the cleanliness of spoon etc.
It is further stated that it was the duty of the prosecution to prove these facts.
These arguments were also addressed before the trial court.
The relevant part of the judgment dealing with these arguments are from para 25 to 48 of the judgment.
11 As far as the arguments in this regard is concerned, the law discussed by the trial court is correct and the same is self explanatory.
However, as far as the analysis of facts are concerned, to my opinion, the same requires some more elaboration.
12 As far as Rule 14 of PFA Rules are concerned, it spells out that the FI shall use dry bottles or containers for the purposes of sampling.

However, this fact was elaborated further by Hon. Supreme Court in Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236 stating that "it must be the endeavour of the FI to use clean and dry implements in sampling the articles of food.

entities.text: Varghese Vs. Food, 1989 (II) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If unhygienic methods are adopted, it will effect the result of analysis.
So, the Hon. Supreme Court use the word "implements" instead of only "dry and clean bottles/containers".
Similarly, in other judgments, i.e. State of Haryana Vs. Kishan Kumar CLT 559, it was observed that the prosecution had not stated that the "weighing scale" was clean.

entities.text: State of Haryana Vs. Kishan Kumar CLT 559
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Similarly, in other judgments, like Sardar Mal Jain, 1996 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 203, it was stated that the newspaper on which the Barfi was weighed was not clean.

entities.text: Sardar Mal Jain, 1996 (2) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases, 203
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Similarly, in Shashi Kant Vs. State of UP, 1983 (1)
Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases 90, it was observed that the "bhagona" was not CA No. 20/16 Dinesh Yadav Vs. State page 4 of 6 proved to be clean and dry.

entities.text:
Shashi Kant Vs. State of UP, 1983 (1)
Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases 90
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13 So, accordingly, it can be said that the law which can be crystallized from various judgments of Hon. High Courts as well as Hon. Supreme Court is that if in evidence, the prosecution states that the sample commodity had touched a surface of an "implement" or any other surface, it is the duty of the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that the said implement/surface was clean and dry and thus could not have added any impurity to the sample.
However, it is not the law that the FI shall spell out on which surfaces the sample commodity had touched while sampling.
However, if he chooses to spell out the implements/surfaces with which the sample commodity came into contact/touch, the same must be proved as clean and dry.

R/O 38 vs The State (Delhi Administration) on 14 May, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23115013/
3 14
In the present case, none of the witnesses had stated in their examination-in-chief as to how those Ladoos were picked.
However, all the witnesses have stated that the Ladoos were in a tray.
Thereafter the same were taken in different tray which was clean and dry.
Thereafter, they were crushed with a clean and dry spoon and then weighed.
However in the cross-examination of PW1 dated 12.08.2010 he stated that "the Ladoos were taken with the help of steel plucker by the vendor".

However, to the same fact PW2 in his cross-examination dated 21.01.2011 stated that "the Ladoos were put by vendor with his hands from this tray into another clean and dry steel tray for weighing the same."
Now accordingly, there is contradiction in the statement of both the witnesses regarding the manner in which the Ladoos were taken out the tray (display tray).
Moreover, none of the witnesses had stated that the plucker or the hands of the vendor were clean and dry and free from colour.
CA No. 20/16 Dinesh Yadav Vs. State  15
So, in these circumstances, the prosecution failed to prove the strict compliance u/sec.14 of PFA Rules.
16 So, the judgment and order on sentence of the trial court is reversed.
17 Accused Dinesh Yadav is acquitted of the charges u/sec.16(1A) read with sec.7 of PFA Act.
18 Bail Bond u/sec.437A Cr.P.C. already furnished.
Accepted for six months.
19 TCR be sent back with copy of the order.
20 File of appeal be consigned to Record Room.
ANNOUNCED
In the open Court (RAKESH PANDIT)
New Delhi District
Patiala House Courts/New Delhi CA No. 20/16 Dinesh Yadav Vs. State  Dinesh Yadav Vs.
